solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Support police trap involving yarn or treacherous activity

parts.note: to back is to support

indicators.note: involving means the trap's word wraps round the yarn's word

parts.note: a sting is an undercover police trap
abb is a weaving yarn, the weft

explanation.surface: A police sting built around some yarn, or a betrayal: the reader wonders what the support has to do with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts the yarn inside the trap to make STABBING. Abb is a Chambers word for the weft yarn in weaving. 'or' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stabbing someone in the back is the idiom for betrayal, so the noun names treacherous conduct.

clue.text: Marmot that's died in overturned old carriage

indicators.note: in means the death abbreviation sits inside the carriage word
overturned in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a cab, short for cabriolet, was a horse-drawn carriage
OB is short for obiit, Latin for 'died'

explanation.surface: A marmot found dead in an upturned carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns the carriage upside down to BAC, as a down clue reads; 'in' puts the death abbreviation inside it. OB is short for Latin obiit, seen on gravestones.
explanation.definitionFit: The bobac is a species of marmot found on the steppes of eastern Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Motor vehicle on old track, a passable country lane?

parts.note: a car is a motor vehicle
troad is an obsolete (Spenserian) word for a track or path

explanation.surface: A car driving along an old track, asking whether the country lane is passable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word. TROAD is an old spelling of trod, a path.
explanation.definitionFit: A cart road is a rough way fit for carts, so the question mark allows a country lane that vehicles can use.

clue.text: Togs changed when operation's involved? Such a policy varies a lot

definitions.text: Such a policy varies a lot

indicators.note: involved means the operation's letters are taken into the middle of the rearranged clothes
changed means the letters of togs are rearranged

parts.note: togs are clothes; here only its letters matter
OP is the usual abbreviation for operation

explanation.surface: Clothes are swapped when an operation is involved, and some policy keeps changing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges TOGS as STGO, and 'involved' takes OP into it to make ST-OP-GO. 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop-go economic policy alternates between restraint and expansion, so it changes direction often.

clue.text: Poet's ultimate rule with poem penning — does it facilitate meeting of minds?

definitions.text: does it facilitate meeting of minds?

indicators.note: ultimate means the last letter of poet

parts.note: the word poet supplies its final letter

indicators.note: penning means the poem's word encloses the rule's letter

parts.note: an elegy is a poem of lament

explanation.surface: A poet ends up writing an elegy under some rule, wondering whether minds can meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimate' gives T, the end of poet; 'penning' puts R inside ELEGY to make ELERGY. 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Telergy is the supposed force at work in telepathy, communication straight from one mind to another.

clue.text: Indian merchant? One favoured tree climbing

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: a means one
to be in is to be in favour
tree is an archaic word for the gallows, and nub is obsolete slang for the gallows

explanation.surface: An Indian merchant who, as a favoured man, climbs a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reads A, IN and NUB from the bottom up. Both 'tree' and NUB are old words for the gallows.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunnia (or bania) is a Hindu trader or shopkeeper in India; the question mark flags the less familiar spelling.

clue.text: Spots weak points in book — plenty

definitions.meaning: a blot is a weak point, as an exposed piece in backgammon

parts.note: lots means plenty

explanation.surface: Someone spots the weak points in a book, and there are plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions and wordplay: B for book, then LOTS for plenty; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A blot is both a stain on a surface and a vulnerable spot, as an unprotected piece in backgammon.

clue.text: Sung prince, I succeed king

parts.note: to go is to succeed, as in 'make a go of it'
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A prince in an opera announces that he will succeed the king.
explanation.walkthrough: Borodin's opera Prince Igor makes him a prince who is sung.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Igor is the title role of Borodin's opera, so he is a prince whose part is sung on stage.

clue.text: Former monarch watches tons, duller than the rest

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, any of the King Georges
to eye is to watch, so eyes means watches

explanation.surface: A deposed king watches tons of something, the dullest of the lot.
explanation.walkthrough: GR, the royal cipher of King George, is a common crossword monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Greyest is the superlative of grey, meaning dull or drab, so it means drabber than all the others.

clue.text: Circle, a constituent in illusory paintings? (5, two words)

parts.note: O is the shape of a circle
a part is a constituent

explanation.surface: A circle as one element in paintings that trick the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' and 'in' are link words. The answer is two words, OP ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is abstract art that uses geometric patterns to create optical illusions.

clue.text: Papa, on hair appearing in a new way: 'It's a sign of puberty'?

indicators.note: appearing in a new way means the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hair appearing on a boy, which his father reads as a sign of puberty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing in a new way' rearranges the letters of PAPA ON HAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraphonia is an alteration of the voice, such as the breaking of a boy's voice at puberty.

clue.text: SE European as is common having leader replaced by British

indicators.note: having leader replaced by means the first letter of the word for common is swapped for the British letter

parts.note: vulgar means common, of the ordinary people

explanation.surface: A south-east European who is common, until a British leader takes over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having leader replaced by' swaps the V of VULGAR for B.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulgar is an old name for a Bulgarian, a native of a country in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: A friend, one left out before dark? That can be explained

parts.note: the article a becomes an before a vowel, so 'A friend' is 'an ally'

indicators.note: out means one left-letter is removed from the friend's word

parts.note: an ally is a friend
L is the abbreviation for left, and one of them goes
sable means black or dark, in poetry and heraldry

explanation.surface: A friend leaves before nightfall, and that can be explained.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is reading 'A' as the article's other form, since it changes before a vowel; 'out' then drops one of the friend's two Ls, leaving ALY. 'before' is a link word; sable is the heraldic word for black.
explanation.definitionFit: Something analysable can be broken down and examined, so it is capable of being explained.

clue.text: Floral decoration in pub a lout knocked over

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: knocked over means a lout is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a lob is a lout or clumsy oaf

explanation.surface: A lout in a pub knocks over the floral display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns 'a lout' round to BOLA once the lout is read as lob, an old word for a clumsy oaf. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbola is a craft of modelling flowers and fruit in paste to decorate objects.

clue.text: Work in tea cropping advanced plantation

indicators.note: in means the work's letters go inside what is left of the drink
cropping means the advanced letter is cut from the drink's word

parts.note: the word tea, which loses a letter
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Work in a tea plantation, cropping the leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cropping' cuts the advanced letter from the drink to leave TE, and 'in' puts the work inside. OP (opus) is the usual crossword word for a work.
explanation.definitionFit: A tope is an Indian word for a grove or plantation of trees, especially mangoes.

clue.text: Fashionable, arty works — one receives mail arriving first

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: works means the letters of arty are set to work, rearranged

explanation.surface: Fashionable, arty works receive first mail.
explanation.walkthrough: IN, then 'works' rearranges ARTY as TRAY.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-tray on a desk is where incoming letters land first, before being dealt with.

clue.text: The old get anxious, it being missing from motorist's tools?

indicators.note: being missing from means the word it is taken out of the tool kit

parts.note: a car kit is a motorist's tool kit

explanation.surface: A motorist worries about missing tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being missing from' takes IT out of CARKIT. 'The old' marks an archaic verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Cark is an archaic verb meaning to fret or worry, so it is old usage for becoming anxious.

clue.text: Poet's train is led astray about opening of poem

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the poem's first letter
astray means the letters are led off course, rearranged

parts.note: the letters of is led

indicators.note: opening of means the first letter of poem

parts.note: the word poem supplies its first letter

explanation.surface: A poet's train of thought is led astray at the start of a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' rearranges IS LED as DISLE; 'opening of' gives P; 'about' puts DISLE round P. 'Poet's' marks a Spenserian word.
explanation.definitionFit: Disple is Spenser's word for discipline, so in his usage it means to train or chastise.

clue.text: Material for milady's shoes, range in hide once old

indicators.note: in means the range sits inside the hide

parts.note: pell is an obsolete word for a skin or hide
a run is a range, as of a stretch of ground

explanation.surface: A lady's shoes made from an old hide with a range of material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the range inside the hide to make PRUNELL. 'once' marks the hide word as obsolete; the final O is for old.
explanation.definitionFit: Prunello is a strong silk or woollen stuff once used for the uppers of women's shoes.

clue.text: Botanist examines it minutely — dog romps excitedly round it locally

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters surround the dialect pronoun
excitedly means the letters romp about, rearranged

parts.note: the letters of dog romps
a is a dialect form of the pronoun it

explanation.surface: A botanist peers closely while a dog romps around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitedly' rearranges DOG ROMPS as SPODOGRM, and 'round' puts it around A to give SPODOGR-A-M.
explanation.definitionFit: A spodogram is the ash skeleton of a plant left after burning, studied under a microscope.

clue.text: Crush, constant with race getting into school

indicators.note: getting into means the constant and race go inside the school's letters

parts.note: sch. is how dictionaries shorten school, as in a school's name on a sports fixture list
C is the physicists' symbol for a constant (the speed of light), with run, a race, beside it

explanation.surface: A crush at school when a race is on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting into' signals insertion: the constant and the race go inside SCH. C is the physicists' symbol for the speed of light.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrunch something is to crush or crumple it.

clue.text: Storm: what'll one do about damaged map?

indicators.note: about means the fury surrounds the rearranged map

parts.note: faced with a damaged map, one will rage

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of map are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone storms off, asking what to do about a ruined map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges the map as AMP, and 'about' puts the fury round it. 'Storm' looks like a noun, but it is the verb, as in storming about.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush about violently, to storm around.

clue.text: Dreary pedant — one confined to study's working after small dram

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for dram

indicators.note: confined to means the single letter is kept inside the rearranged letters
working means the letters are set to work, rearranged

parts.note: the letters of study's
a means one

explanation.surface: A dull scholar shut away in a study, working after a tot of whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: The dram's abbreviation comes first ('after' is a link word here); 'working' rearranges the letters of study's as YSDUST, and 'confined to' locks the one inside to make YASDUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Dryasdust is a dull, pedantic antiquary from Scott's prefaces, and his name became a word for any boring scholar.

clue.text: Sound of guns, worrying rattle one with frequency apprehended

indicators.note: apprehended means the one and frequency are caught inside the rattle

parts.note: a rale is an abnormal rattling sound in the chest, a worrying sign
a means one

explanation.surface: The sound of gunfire: a worrying rattle heard again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apprehended' catches A and F inside RALE after its R. 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rafale is a burst of artillery fire, a rapid series of shots.

clue.text: Curve like this limits rising rent

indicators.note: limits means the Latin word encloses the reversed tear

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, so, like this

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a rip is a rent or tear

explanation.surface: A curve like this marks the limit of rising rents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reads the tear upwards as PIR, as a down clue goes, and 'limits' puts the Latin word round it. Sic is the Latin for thus, used in quotations.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiric is the curve formed by a plane section of a torus.

clue.text: One of the anglers upright on sides of Dee

indicators.note: on sides of means the upright type is placed either side of the letter

parts.note: roman type is upright, as against italic
Dee is the spelt-out name of the letter D

explanation.surface: An angler stands upright on the banks of the River Dee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dee' looks like the river; here it is just the letter D, and 'on sides of' puts ROMAN either side of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodman is someone who fishes with a rod, an angler.

clue.text: Rock resident, ancient character brought up on principle of thrift

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: ogam (ogham) is the ancient Celtic alphabet, so one of its characters

indicators.note: principle of means the first letter, from Latin principium, beginning

parts.note: the word thrift supplies its first letter

explanation.surface: A rock dweller, brought up on an ancient thrifty principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reads OGAM upwards as MAGO, and 'principle of' gives T from thrift. 'on' is a link word. The Rock is Gibraltar.
explanation.definitionFit: The magot is the Barbary ape, the tailless macaque that lives on the Rock of Gibraltar.

clue.text: Stump made of different metals

parts.note: the first of the different metals is tin, chemical symbol Sn
the second of the metals is silver, chemical symbol Ag

explanation.surface: A tree stump said to be made of different metals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different metals' asks for two metal symbols side by side: tin, then silver. 'made of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is a jagged stump of a branch or tree sticking out.

clue.text: Lecherous attempt aiming for lady's rear

parts.note: a go is an attempt
to be at something is to aim for it

indicators.note: rear means the last letter

parts.note: the word lady supplies its last letter

explanation.surface: A lecherous man aims a pass at a lady's behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rear' takes the last letter of lady, Y. 'aiming for' gives AT, as in 'getting at'.
explanation.definitionFit: Goats are traditionally symbols of lust, so goaty means lustful, lecherous.

clue.text: With lack of good evidence thus lots're set free — as true felons?

indicators.note: set free means the letters of lots're are let out of the felons' letters, and what remains is rearranged

parts.note: the letters of as true felons
the letters of lots're, which are removed

explanation.surface: A verdict quashed for lack of evidence, freeing many who were felons after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set free' takes LOTSRE out of ASTRUEFELONS, and the rest is rearranged. 'thus' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsafe conviction is one the court finds unreliable, typically because the evidence was not good enough.

clue.text: Indicating a complete lack of hospitals

definitions.meaning: second meaning: plural of san, short for sanatorium

explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word between two meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition means entirely without, and the noun is the plural of a short form for sanatoria.

clue.text: Means to drain measure of port?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tube carrying away water
second meaning: a large cask, a measure of wine such as port

explanation.walkthrough: Port suggests a harbour, but here it is the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A drainpipe carries off water, and a pipe is also a cask holding about 105 gallons of wine.

clue.text: Lichen yielding dye? Cut the lot back

parts.note: to pare is to cut

indicators.note: back means the word for the lot is read backwards

parts.note: all means the lot

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a dye-yielding lichen should be cut right back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns 'the lot' round to LLA. 'Cut ... back' reads as pruning, but the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Parella is a crustose lichen once used to make the purple dye archil.

clue.text: Cooking oil, one contained in nut tree

indicators.note: contained in means the one goes inside the tree's name

parts.note: cola (kola) is the tree that bears cola nuts
an means one

explanation.surface: Cooking oil pressed from a single nut tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contained in' puts the one inside the tree. The nut tree is not the source of the oil; canola comes from rapeseed.
explanation.definitionFit: Canola is a variety of rapeseed bred for low acidity, whose oil is widely used in cooking.

clue.text: Feature of coastline where imp goes ford seashell?

parts.note: read as a question, it asks where to put imp to make a seashell; the reply is in the word let, giving limpet

explanation.surface: A coastline feature, where an imp wanders along the shore past seashells.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer IN LET: putting IMP in LET gives LIMPET, a seashell. 'ford' as given here reads as 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlet is a narrow arm of the sea running into the land, a common shoreline feature.

clue.text: Mothers etc with yen twice suffering what no husbands can undergo

indicators.note: suffering means all these letters are put through it, rearranged

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for yen, the Japanese currency, taken twice

explanation.surface: Mothers and the like suffering, twice over, an operation no husband could have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges MOTHERS, ETC and two Ys; 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A hysterectomy is surgical removal of the womb, which men lack, so no husband can have one.
